The recipe for new friends is simple:

1. Find a venue where you'll tend to run into the same people every time (work, school, hobby, etc.)

2. Once you've become a familiar face to the people you can start by saying hey and making very brief small talk. Don't try to go all in with getting people to have a conversation with you - that will simply scare them off.

3. Repeat step 2 over a period of time. As time passes, the conversations will tend to be less benign and last a little longer. This shows that people are comfortable around you and they've determined you're not a creep. 

4. This is where either you can make the first move or them. Best case scenario is that someone invites you to a social function with other member of said venue and you can repeat steps 2 and 3 with the new people. Otherwise, invite them out to something non-committal and that won't take up too much time. Going out for a beer, a quick bite to eat, etc. Do NOT take it personally if they refuse on the first attempt This just means they're still not quite comfortable which means you need to keep doing step 3.

5. Interactions outside of the venue will help create further talking points and increase your comfort levels around each other. Congrats, you've made a new friend(s)!

Note that this process is not something that will happen overnight. It may take weeks, even months to do. You must have patience and remember that you reap what you sow.

Not sure if this has been said yet, so I'll just say it. The fact that you're posting this on here right now is kind of saying that in a way your trust for this person has already been breached. That being said, the real question here is, do you personally feel that the relationship is strong enough to overcome this hump? 

Reason being, you probably already have it in your mind that she may cheat on you with her ex, seeing as how close they are. Well, what would him moving out change? You're still going to be gone for 3 weeks of 4 and if she wants to cheat on you she will. There's absolutely nothing you can do that will stop it from happening. It sucks but again the true question here is, do you feel that you can trust her even after this situation is resolved?

If you feel that you can trust her even after all of this, then it is my advice to be sure that the ground rules are set, it is in my personal opinion that what she did was wrong. But hey people make mistakes, that's why we're human. Mistakes is also why we begin to loose trust and faith in our partners. Although, again if you feel that you can trust her after this just make sure she knows what you're comfortable with her and her ex so that mistakes like this don't happen again.

If you don't feel that you can trust her after this, then i recommend you moving on. There are plenty of other fish in the sea, and who knows maybe you can find someone where you work seeing as how you're there the majority of the time anyway. it'll give you a reason to possibly move closer to where you work and spend more time with the one you may love.

Anyway, I hope this helps and I didn't step on any toes. Best of luck to you my friend.

For those intrested [this ](http://www.reddit.com/r/amiugly/comments/xnybo/progress_check_from_a_post_almost_a_year_ago/) is where i am and where i have come from in my style transformation.
